clue.text: Spots artists at hospital

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, so artists gives RAS
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital on road signs and maps

explanation.surface: Painters seen at a hospital, perhaps with a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red marks on the skin, which people call spots.

clue.text: Outstanding charts?

parts.note: outstanding is read literally as standing out in raised form, describing maps with three-dimensional terrain

explanation.definitionFit: Relief maps show hills and valleys raised from the surface, so their features literally stand out.

clue.text: Desperate ant sipped — from this?

indicators.note: desperate suggests a frantic, disordered state, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A thirsty insect drinks from a street water tap.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a desperate ant might drink from a public tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpipe is an outdoor water pipe with a tap, the kind someone parched might drink from.

clue.text: Sharp razor helps with this narrow escape

explanation.surface: A keen blade gives a clean shave, and a near miss is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen blade gives a very near shave of the skin, and the same phrase is the idiom for a lucky near miss.

clue.text: See bass crooner throwing up

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
B is the abbreviation for bass in music
Bing Crosby was the famous crooner

explanation.surface: Watch a deep-voiced singer being sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing up' is not vomiting but tossing a ball high, as in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobbing means tossing something in a high arc, so throwing it upwards.

clue.text: Snake makes a funny present

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters of the next word appear in a strange order

explanation.surface: A snake would be an amusing gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a literary word for a snake.

clue.text: Labour's leader is sentimental about part of the body

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged
a leader comes first, so this takes the opening letter of the party name

explanation.surface: Labour's leader gets mushy about some anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges L (the first letter of Labour's) plus IS and SENTIMENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The small intestine is the long digestive tube between the stomach and the colon.

clue.text: Fruit in a cereal

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A fruit found in a bowl of breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of an oak, which botanists classify as a fruit.

clue.text: Prime minister's garden

explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was British PM in 1955 to 1957, and Eden is the biblical paradise garden of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: The hardware shop is good for this small present

definitions.text: The hardware shop is good for this

explanation.surface: An ironmonger is the place to find a little Christmas gift.
explanation.walkthrough: A hardware shop stocks goods and fills its stock, so it is literally a stocking filler.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocking filler is a cheap gift placed in a Christmas stocking; a shop that stocks goods fills its stock.

clue.text: Jumped for exercise at the field

indicators.note: at places the exercise right beside, after, the field

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone leapt about doing exercise out in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is the past tense of leap, a synonym of jumped.

clue.text: Italian song about girl having no clothes on!

indicators.note: about means the naked word is wrapped around the girl's name

parts.note: having no clothes on means bare
Carol is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A risqué Italian song about a girl who is naked.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark points at the saucy surface; 'about' is the container signal, wrapping the naked word around the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a Venetian gondolier's song, so an Italian song in origin.

clue.text: Cooked cod in Greenland provides part of the body

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of the following words are doctored or rearranged

explanation.surface: Fish prepared in Greenland turns out to contain an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges all fourteen letters of COD IN GREENLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: An endocrine gland, such as the thyroid, is an organ secreting hormones into the blood, one part of human anatomy.

clue.text: Civil servants, perhaps, jail drug-dealers

parts.note: pen is American slang for a penitentiary, a jail
pushers are people who sell drugs

explanation.surface: Bureaucrats might lock up those selling narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-pushers is a dismissive term for clerks doing routine office paperwork, such as some civil servants.

clue.text: Sending mum one type of heather

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
I is the Roman numeral one
ling is the common heather, Calluna

explanation.surface: Posting one's mother a sprig of heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Mailing something is posting or dispatching it.

clue.text: Board taking in points can be defended

indicators.note: taking in means the board word holds the points inside it

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging
E and N are compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: A committee board considers points that it could justify.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be held or maintained against attack.

clue.text: Bishop in front of bell using a jokey tone

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ante is Latin for before, in front of
to ring is to call on the telephone, as in give someone a bell

explanation.surface: A bishop stands before the church bell, speaking playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantering means exchanging teasing, playful remarks.

clue.text: Promised to install shelf in the American police department

indicators.note: install ... in means the shelf word is put inside the police letters

parts.note: PD is the abbreviation for an American police department, as in NYPD
a ledge is a shelf

explanation.surface: An officer promised to put a shelf up in a US police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledged means vowed or gave one's word, a synonym of promised.

clue.text: Formal bearing senior person displays without having a right to it

indicators.note: without having means the letters for a right are removed

parts.note: a dignitary is a person of high rank
A plus R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A grandee carries himself with poise despite not deserving it.
explanation.walkthrough: DIGNITARY loses its A and R to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignity is a composed, stately manner, a formal bearing.

clue.text: Make tidy — profit?

explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is to put things in order, and also slang for making a large gain or killing on a deal.

clue.text: Sailing boat contains learner's mess

indicators.note: contains means the boat word holds the learner letter

parts.note: a cutter is a single-masted sailing boat
L is the learner plate on British cars

explanation.surface: A trainee sailor makes a mess aboard a small yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: Clutter is untidy mess, a jumble of things lying about.

clue.text: Support using a plane — except with lock on

parts.note: flying is travelling by aeroplane
but means except, as in all but one
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Air travel is fine, except when your hair is caught up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' is architectural: the arched prop on Gothic cathedrals.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying buttress is an arched external prop holding up the wall of a large building.

clue.text: Ascends without use of front legs, perhaps

indicators.note: without use of front means the opening letter of the climbing word is dropped

parts.note: climbs means ascends

explanation.surface: A climber goes up using only legs, not the arms in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Legs are examples of limbs, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Tart helping, looking back, to some abdication

indicators.note: looking back means the run is read from right to left
helping means a portion, so a run of letters is taken from inside the word

explanation.surface: A tart is shared out, some going to an abdicating monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' takes DICA from abdication; 'looking back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid means sour or sharp-tasting, like tart.

clue.text: Minor ailment is cause for an expression of disappointment

explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be a mild illness or a grumble voicing dissatisfaction.

clue.text: Hum is a smell about one

indicators.note: about means the smell word goes round the numeral

parts.note: nose is a wine taster's word for a smell or aroma
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A humming sound is accompanied by a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A hum is a low continuous sound, one kind of noise.

clue.text: They damage warships

explanation.definitionFit: Destroyers are vandals who wreck things, and also fast naval escort vessels.

clue.text: Wise men don't start being so for years

indicators.note: don't start means the opening letter of the word for wise men is dropped

parts.note: sages are wise men

explanation.surface: Sages are not born wise; it takes them years.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages, as in waiting for ages, means a very long time, many years.
